extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers interested in wartime/military news (WWII-era audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting on Allied and Axis military operations and their effects for a general newspaper audience; combines official communiqués, pilot/eyewitness quotes, reconnaissance evidence, and strategic context to convey scale and significance of actions. Typically produced as Associated Press/British press dispatches during WWII.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution to official sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Report and attribute major claims to named official sources (e.g., "the Air Ministry communique", "The Eighth United States Air Force communique", "the German High Command", radio broadcasts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always cite the issuing organization when reporting numbers, damage assessments or operational claims; identify when information is preliminary or comes from enemy broadcasts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative operational details
rubrics_metrics.description: Include specific numerical information such as numbers of bombers used or lost (e.g., "43 big bombers" lost; "the biggest force of heavy bombers of the war"), tons of bombs dropped (e.g., "undoubtedly exceeded the record 2,000 tons loosed on Dortmund"), and counts of buildings/acreage damaged (e.g., "150 acres have been totally devastated").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide exact figures where available, note estimates, and indicate if the actual number was not announced; use comparative figures for scale (previous raids, records).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify primary and secondary targets with geographic specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Name the principal objective(s) and secondary targets and give precise geographic markers (city names, rivers, distances — e.g., "Duesseldorf was the main objective..."; "Muenster, 60 miles northeast of Duesseldorf on the Ems river").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish main objectives from secondary targets and give place names and relative locations so readers can understand strategic context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of returning airmen/eyewitness quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Include vivid first-hand descriptions from returning pilots and crew (e.g., weather over target "perfect", bombs "touched off fires visible for 70 miles", personal action accounts like Sgt. McDermott's dogfight description).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed short direct quotes from servicemen to convey immediacy and human perspective; attribute rank and hometown when given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconnaissance / photographic evidence for damage assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Base and report damage estimates on reconnaissance photographs and official reviews (e.g., "Reconnaissance photographs showed..."; listing of destroyed/damaged buildings based on photos).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite aerial reconnaissance as the basis for damage tallies and note limitations (areas not yet photographed, difficulty distinguishing old vs new damage).

rubrics_metrics.name: Present opposing/propaganda claims and note contradictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Report enemy claims (e.g., German radio/High Command declaring British and U.S. aircraft shot down) alongside Allied accounts, and indicate where accounts conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give both sides' statements, label enemy broadcasts as such, and flag discrepancies or areas where claims cannot be independently verified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualize attacks historically and comparatively
rubrics_metrics.description: Place each raid in a temporal and comparative context (e.g., "fifty-third raid on Duesseldorf", "largest force since 1,250 R.A.F. bombers in 1942", references to earlier May 23 or March raids).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include prior-raid counts and notable milestones to show escalation, frequency, and cumulative effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report civilian and infrastructure impact explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: List civilian structures and infrastructure damaged or destroyed (e.g., power station, telegraph office, fire station, housing counts) and quantify where possible (e.g., "at least 1,258 houses were destroyed or damaged").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail effects on civilian life and municipal services, giving counts and naming key facilities to show humanitarian and logistical consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report military/strategic interpretation and statements by commanders
rubrics_metrics.description: Include statements or orders from military leadership that explain intent or tactics (e.g., "Air Marshal Sir Arthur T. Harris... ordered the raid", references to "softening-up blows", "imminence of invasion" stressed by commentators).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute strategic explanations to named leaders or official communiqués and summarize the stated military purpose or anticipated effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note operational conditions and opposition encountered
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe operational environment details such as weather, fighter opposition, anti-aircraft fire, and escort status (e.g., "weather... perfect", "lightest yet encountered in the Ruhr", "unescorted trip").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report environmental and enemy-resistance factors that affected the mission and losses, using returning crew statements and official reports.
